This  document,  the  Owner's  Technical  Specification  Part  B  (OTS  Part  B)  defines  requirements  for  the engineering, procurement and construction of each of Rumah and Nairyah IPPs that the Contractor shall comply with, which are in addition to those specified in OTS Part A.
In addition to the technical requirements of this section, the selection of the technology, the design and the arrangement of the Power Units shall be based on the site conditions as described in OTS Part A.
The Plant shall be designed, manufactured and configured in such a way as to optimise Plant performance, thus providing  a  competitive  least  cost  electricity  generation  taking  into  account  the  design  and  operation requirements of this OTS, Part A and Part B.
The Plant shall be designed, manufactured, installed and be suitable in every respect for continuous operation at the Guaranteed Net Contracted Power Capacity 1,800 MW ± 5% (GNCPC) at part loads, under the anticipated transient operation as well as the climatic conditions and the site environmental restrictions and shall exhibit high availability and reliability. Please refer to  section 6.4 for the Availability Reliability and Maintainability statement. In order to demonstrate the availability and reliability, the Contractor shall perform a RAM study.
The Plant shall be designed to permit unconstrained operation over the full range of ambient conditions. The Plant  shall  have  operationally  flexible  power  capacity  that  will  play  a  key  role  in  providing  flexible  power generation.
All the sections below (this documentPart B) define the Owner's requirements for the configuration of the Plant in addition to that specified in OTS Part A. OTS Part A shall generally have the priority over OTS Part B. In case of any requirement specified in OTS Part B found to be in contradiction with the requirements stated in OTS Part A,  the  conservative  and  stringent  requirement  of  them  will  prevail  in  addition  to  the  compliance  of  the requirement stated in Part A.

Vent-holes and drain-holes should be provided to avoid high internal pressures and air-locks during immersion, which may cause explosions, and to ensure that molten zinc is not retained in pockets during withdrawal.

The surface of the steelwork to be galvanized shall be free from paint, oil, grease and similar contaminants in accordance with DIN 55928, part 4 and DIN 50976. Structural steel items shall be initially grit-blasted to B.S. 4232, second quality, (Sa 21/2) or by pickling in a bath and the minimum average coating weight on steel sections 5 mm thick and over shall be 900 g/m2.

Galvanized contact surfaces to be joined by high-tensile friction-grip bolts shall be roughened before assembly so that the required slip factor (defined in B.S. 3294, part 1 and B.S. 4604, part 1) is achieved. - Low  alloy  steels  containing  ½  per  cent  molybdenum  and  1¼  per  cent  chromium,  ½  per  cent molybdenum up to and including thicknesses of 12.5 mm provided that:

- Low alloy steels not containing vanadium, 5 minutes per mm of thickness with a minimum time of 120 minutes
- Low  alloy  steels  containing  vanadium  and  high  (11  to  15  per  cent)  chromium  steels  containing vanadium, 180 minutes regardless of thickness

The requirements for post weld heat treatment do not affect or replace in any way the requirements for maintenance of welding preheats or post welding heating for the purposes of diffusing hydrogen from the weldment.

A fully integrated, DCS shall be provided to monitor, control, display, alarm and record selected physical and electrical parameters associated with all plant areas.
The Plant (each Unit) shall be operated, monitored and controlled from a Control Room (CR).

- Allow for automatic control of all the systems of the Plant from the CR,
- Ability to collect signals and alarms from all the necessary systems.
- Critical  signals  shall  have  a  minimum  level  of  redundancy  to  guarantee  reliability  and availability of the Plant in any circumstance.
- Provision of a remote monitoring system and software with supervisory role and access to historic values.
- This shall include 2 web based monitoring for Offtake connection along with any license required.
- Remote access shall be allowed for maintenance and backup purpose.
The system shall be designed to have a functionally and geographically distributed architecture utilising a number of independent outstations. The equipment located in the DCS cubicles shall include all necessary control processors, input/output (I/O) cards, power supplies, data highway interfaces and termination facilities.
The microprocessor-based distributed control system shall comprise of multifunctional modules operating over a network. The operators have access to all significant process information and all controls Analogue and Digital signal will have separate cables. Analogue cables are twisted pair and screen protected.
Outstations shall be capable of autonomous operation and perform data acquisition, calculation, digital (open loop) and analogue (closed-loop) control functions.
Operator's workstations shall allow monitoring, control and adjustment of Plant operation conditions via highresolution 'windows' style graphics displays. All VDUs, keyboards, printers and peripheral devices and their associated control desks shall be supplied.
One 72' large screen graphics wall monitor for the plant shall be provided in the CCR which will primarily be used for:
- I. Display of important data and graphics from the DCS, video, etc.;
- II. To provide real time clear luminous information to operators and visitors;
- III. The whole screen of the large screen graphics wall should behave as a single logical screen and the control of the same shall be from a dedicated graphical control unit having a keyboard and mouse. However, as an option it should be possible to control the Graphics Wall from a PC on LAN having Windows NT/2000 OS;
The complete system shall be interfaced on 10/100 MBPS LAN as a minimum. Provision for additional VDU shall be provided for future additions. The man machine interface shall be to the review and approval of the Owner in accordance with the Contract. The display screens shall be developed in conjunction with the Owner and shall be to the review and approval of the Owner in accordance with the Contract.

The response times for the Operator's workstations under normal conditions shall be as follows:
The DCS, as finally configured and installed, shall exhibit response times which do not adversely impact the operation of plant equipment nor impede the operator's response to events. To this end the maximum response times defined within this specification shall not be exceeded.
- a) Control  response  time  is  defined  as  the  elapsed  time  between  the  moment  a  signal  change  is originated at the input card of a processing unit until a controller action takes place in another processing  station,  assuming  the  worst  communication  situation  possible,  including  maximum data highway traffic level, longest cable length and largest access time to the data highway. This time shall not exceed the following values:
- i. Slow Loops 1000 millisecond (such as temperatures and large tank levels)
- ii. Fast Loops 500 millisecond (such as most flows and some pressures)
- iii. Discrete/Logic Control 500 millisecond (motor control/interlocks)
- b) Monitoring function response time is defined as the time between initiation of an action or event and the time at which the operator is advised of the event through a LCD display or a printer output. These times include the elements of the control response times, including consideration of worst case communications, as well as the additional delays associated with operator station equipment such  as  LCD  buffers,  display  drivers,  and  memory  access.  These  times  shall  not  exceed  the following values:
- i. Operator  Commands  to  Equipment  1000  millisecond  (exclusive  of  external equipment reaction times)
- ii. Alarms/Annunciation  1000  millisecond  (including  pre-processing  for  alarm suppression)
- c) The time between selection and display of a VDU, fully updated, from the database shall not exceed 2 seconds with a typical workstation loading of 4 graphic displays, 2 trends and 1 alarm display in 'windows' on the VDU.
- d) The time between the occurrence and change of a signal at the origin and the change of state, value or alarm showing on the VDU shall not exceed 2 seconds.

The common Plant system shall be DCS-based, with incorporated display hierarchy and display selection concept as follows:
•, 1 = Power Block Overview level,. • Functional area, 1 = Area level control,. • Mechanical units, 1 = Group/Unit level control.. • Components, 1 = Item level control

Operator communication and monitoring shall be carried out via monitors providing the window(s) to the process.
The display layout of an operator station shall be as follows:
- A frame with header and footer is always visible. It contains selection fields for displays and additional information as well as collective displays, which shall also indicate faults in displays not currently visible,
- Basis diagrams occupy the rest of the screen. They provide information on the process in the form of plant diagrams, curves, characteristics, etc.
- Windows  are  selected  in  addition  to  the  basic  diagrams.  Normally  the  window  is  allocated  to  a particular object, e.g. pumps, and provides detailed additional information in graphic or alphanumeric representation.

The  displays  shall  present  process  sequences  and  statuses  in  a  functionally related manner. This shall be achieved by means of three types of displays with different information content, such as:
- o Plant displays which show the physical items in the plant such as pumps, fans, valves, etc. and their  state  by  the  means  of  the  symbol,  colour,  blinking,  (in  acc.  to  DIN  2481)  to  facilitate operator intervention,
- o Representations of physical and technical relationships in form of curves, characteristics, bar graphs,  digital  displays,  to  provide  a  view  the  process.  They  provide  the  operator  with historical, current and forecast states of process.
- o Control system displays showing function diagrams for instrumentation and control as well as device configuration diagrams.
- o Step-bystep indication of sequences' progress and permissive awaited.
The above shall be available whether a DCMS vendor's outstation or packaged plant vendor's PLC provides control.
These different types shall mutually supplement each other and can be called up by the plant personnel in accordance with their access authority. Mixed displays shall be possible.

The DCMS shall incorporate an alarm system with the main tasks of providing a comprehensive and clearly arranged representation of faults in the power plant, facilitating quick localisation of the plant sections affected by faults.
There shall be a Common Alarm Display facilitating blinking marks in diagrams, menus and the overview single lines permanently displayed. Signal disturbances from the complete plant, regardless of the current display and operator control situation, shall b e indicated at the operator's workstation.

- Alarm class; and

Alarm management shall be based on Alarm EEMUA 191 guidelines.

The main parameters of the relay, or relay circuit are:
- i. the  setting  of  the  relay  which  depending  on  the  type  of  relay  concerned,  may  be  a percent, current or voltage value;
- ii. the  value  of  the  stabilising  resistor  (applicable  only  when  the  relay  is  of  the  type calibrated in terms of current);
- iii. the values of any shunt resistance, linear or non-linear used for fault setting adjustment and/or peak secondary voltage limitation.
- c) Relay terminals. These are the terminals on the relay to which the internally mounted coil current  components  are  connected.  The  circuit  between  these  terminals  thus  excludes  any  externally mounted components such as series stabilising resistors and linear and non-linear shunt resistors, which may be provided.
- d) Relay circuit terminals . These are the points at which the relay circuit leads join the leads which  connect  the  current  transformers  in  parallel.  The  relay  circuit  thus  indicates  all  the  externally mounted components, such as stabilising resistor and linear and non-linear shunt resistors, connected as in service.
- e) Relay circuit setting current . This is the minimum value of current in the relay circuit, with the relay set at its prescribed setting, to produce operation of the relay.
- f) Relay circuit setting voltage. This is the minimum value of voltage, which must be applied between the relay circuit terminals, with the relay set at its prescribed setting, to produce operation of the relay.
- g) Current transformer "knee-point" .  The "knee-point" of a current transformer marks the upper limit of the roughly linear portion of the secondary winding excitation characteristic and is defined exactly in British practice as the point at which a 10 percent increase in rms exciting voltage produces 50 percent increase in rms exciting current. The excitation characteristic is that determined by applying sinusoidal exciting voltage to the secondary winding with the primary winding on open-circuit. The exciting voltage  and  current  at  the  "knee-point"  are  termed  the  "knee-point  voltage"  and  "knee-point  exciting current" respectively.
